summary: Religious studies scholar Gavin D'Costa studied at Cambridge and Birmingham. He taught at West London Institute of Higher Education (~1985–1988) and became Emeritus Professor of Catholic Theology at the University of Bristol (1993), with visiting posts in Rome.

Gavin Flood, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Lancaster under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. His posts include the University of Wales, Lampeter, University of Stirling, University of Oxford, and Yale-NUS College.
Tibetology scholar Gelek served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998) and held visiting positions at the University of California and the University of Oxford.

Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar Gelek Rinpoche studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell University under teachers including Ling Rinpoche and Trijang Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1965) and founded Jewel Heart (1988).

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, training under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup and Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima.

Historian and Indologist Gen'ichi Yamazaki earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He worked as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (~1964–1970) and was a professor at Kokugakuin University (~1970–2006).

Genchi Kato worked in religious studies and Japanology, studying under Tetsujiro Inoue at the University of Tokyo. He taught at the Imperial Japanese Army, Army War College, University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin University, and Taisho University.

Gendun Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who served as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling (~1977–1997), which he founded alongside Dhagpo Kundreul Ling and Dhagpo Dedrol Ling.

Gendün Chöphel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum, and Drepung monasteries under teachers including Sherab Gyatso and Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1941).

Genjun Sasaki studied at Kyoto University and worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a professor at Otani University (attested 1974–1995) and held visiting professorships at the University of Hamburg (1956) and Harvard University.
Genro Gito was an 18th-century Buddhist studies figure who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and served as the first seat (第一座) at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Komazawa University (~1931–1934) and later served as a professor there from around 1957 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari studied at Waseda University and worked in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor at Kokushikan University and was a professor and later professor emeritus at Rissho University (1980–2020).
Genshu Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and was a dharma heir of Sogaku Daiun Harada.

Genta Ikeda studied at Kyoto University and worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1965–1970) and professor emeritus at Nara University of Education (~1965–1995).
Genzao was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950, training under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren studied at Stockholm University and Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian religious studies, he was Professor of the History of Religions at Uppsala University (1940–1973).

Geoff Childs, a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology, earned his PhD at Indiana University under Tsetan Chonjore. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Australian National University and taught anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 2003–2005).

Geoffrey Barstow works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Hampshire College, Kathmandu University, and the University of Virginia, and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University (~2013).

Geoffrey Goble is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia and Indiana University, and was an assistant professor of religious studies at the University of Oklahoma (attested 2019).
